knowledge_points.title_zh: 监督学习与无监督学习
knowledge_points.description: Distinguish supervised learning (every training sample has a label) from unsupervised learning (training samples have no labels).
learning_objectives: Distinguish supervised from unsupervised learning by whether training samples carry labels.
Classify a learning task as supervised or unsupervised given the data description.
common_misconceptions: Confusing 'produces an output' with 'has labeled training data'.
mastery_criteria: Can correctly classify a task as supervised or unsupervised based on whether the training data is labeled.

knowledge_points.description: A representative lazy learner: predict a test sample by voting (classification) or averaging (regression) over its k nearest training samples; key issues are the choice of k and the distance metric.
learning_objectives: Explain how the choice of k affects model complexity and overfitting.
Compute Minkowski distances (Euclidean p=2, Manhattan p=1) between two points.
common_misconceptions: Believing a smaller k yields a simpler model.
Confusing Euclidean distance with Manhattan distance.
mastery_criteria: Can state the effect of too-small or too-large k and compute Euclidean/Manhattan distance for given points.

knowledge_points.description: Fits a continuous target with a linear function f(x)=w^T x + b by minimizing the mean squared error (least squares); univariate regression has a closed-form solution.
learning_objectives: State that least squares minimizes mean squared error.
Use the closed-form relation b = y_mean - w * x_mean to compute the intercept.
common_misconceptions: Confusing least squares with minimizing the sum of absolute errors (L1).
Believing linear regression is a classification algorithm.
mastery_criteria: Can write the least-squares objective and compute a univariate regression parameter from the closed form.

knowledge_points.description: Applies the sigmoid function to a linear model to produce a probability in (0,1) for binary classification; the log-odds (logit) ln(y/(1-y)) = w^T x + b is linear. It is a classification algorithm despite the name.
learning_objectives: Identify logistic regression as a classification algorithm, not regression.
Explain the sigmoid output range and the odds/logit meaning.
common_misconceptions: Believing logistic regression is a regression algorithm because of its name.
Believing the sigmoid output can be any real number.
mastery_criteria: Can correctly identify logistic regression's algorithm class and explain sigmoid/logit.

knowledge_points.description: An unsupervised clustering algorithm that represents each cluster by the mean of its samples, iterating through: choose k centers, assign samples to the nearest center, update cluster means, and stop when centers no longer change.
learning_objectives: Recount the four iterative steps of K-Means.
Identify K-Means limitations (pre-set k, initialization sensitivity, iteration cost).
common_misconceptions: Believing K-Means can automatically determine the number of clusters.
Believing K-Means is a supervised learning method.
mastery_criteria: Can describe the K-Means steps in the correct order and identify its limitations.
